arguments.explanation: base1 is required to stay undisturbed throughout the run (it is the fixture and is never picked). Its run-start baseline pose was (0.40278,-0.19857,0.02238) at identity orientation; its current pose is (0.41873,-0.22805,0.02237) with a ~30deg yaw component -- a ~0.0335m translation plus a substantial rotation, with no registry tolerance to compare against since base1 has no spec block (so this is judged directly against the instruction's plain 'undisturbed' requirement rather than a numeric registry bound). Believed mechanism: during the u_orange recovery, the gripper's wide-open recovery grasp drove the fingers into physical contact with base1 (confirmed by the MoveIt START_STATE_IN_COLLISION report naming base1 with contact depth up to 0.0091m), and that contact force shifted/rotated the fixture. Re-querying u_brown_placement live now shows u_brown sitting close to its (moved) slot again (~0.012m away), consistent with u_brown having stayed seated in base1's slot while the whole fixture moved out from under it -- i.e. the part itself was likely not independently pushed; the fixture carrying it was.
